Distinguished exact cover from generalised exact cover, and libsolv from libmamba; Algorithm X need not choose the smallest column although that is a useful heuristic.

tech-greedy-fails-approximation.rationale: Reference card OPT <= G + v_next <= 2 max(G, v_max) kept; the 2-approximation proof was re-derived and checked against the Cornell CS 4820 notes and by brute force on 300 random instances. Ratio-greedy unbounded example checked. Graham 1966 confirmed from the BSTJ text (bound 1 + (n - 1)/n' for n processors, giving 2 - 1/m); Christofides 1976 (reprint abstract: ratio strictly below 3/2) and Serdyukov's independent 1976 discovery published 1978 (van Bevern and Slugina 2020); Karlin-Klein-Oveis Gharan (arXiv 2007.01409: randomised 3/2 - epsilon, epsilon > 10^-36; STOC 2021). Verifier correction: the nearest-neighbour bullet stated only the arbitrary-distance worst-tour result; it now adds the metric logarithmic factor (Rosenkrantz, Stearns and Lewis 1977: logarithmic upper and lower bounds) and scopes the worst-tour claim to arbitrary tables. FPTAS statement (polynomial in items and 1/tolerance) matches Ibarra-Kim 1975 (Crossref title) and Wikipedia. No analogy: a survey of guarantees; the car-boot analogy in the previous unit covers the knapsack picture.

analogyReview.scope: All 40 active lessons: 16 analogy callouts (15 added, 1 converted from the baseline maze paragraph) checked for familiar scenario, technical mapping and stated limit, with required facts outside each disclosure; 24 lessons recorded as not needing an analogy, with reasons.

tech-recursion-contracts.rationale: Cinema row-counting analogy maps each person to a call, the front row to the base case and "add one" to the combine step; the stated limit (no automatic termination guarantee, memory per pending call) is correct. Required facts stay outside the callout.

tech-recursion-frames.rationale: Sticky-note pile maps paused tasks to stack frames and newest-first handling to LIFO unwinding; the limit names the fixed CPython recursion allowance and per-frame memory. Correct and not needed for any question.

tech-recursion-costs.rationale: Family-history analogy: researching both parents without notes maps to two un-memoised recursive calls; ancestors shared through cousin marriages map to repeated subproblems; a notebook is memoisation. The limit correctly contrasts irregular real repeats with Fibonacci's regular pattern.

tech-recursion-tail-calls.rationale: Help-desk analogy maps the forgetful hand-off to a tail call that needs no frame afterwards and the file note to the accumulator; the limit states that frame reuse is an implementation property (Scheme yes, C maybe, CPython no). Accurate.

tech-recursion-iteration.rationale: No formula and no analogy needed: a mechanical conversion procedure that the code shows directly.

tech-divide-conquer-structure.rationale: Vote-counting analogy maps districts to independent subproblems and regional/national totals to the combine step; the limit notes a single fixed split and a potentially expensive combine. Accurate; no question depends on it.

tech-divide-conquer-master.rationale: Company analogy maps direct reports to the branching factor a, shrinking shares to b and coordination time to f(n), and illustrates root-, leaf- and equal-dominated totals; the limit restricts the theorem to uniform branching, shrink factor and power-shaped work. Accurate.

tech-divide-conquer-binary.rationale: Phone-book analogy maps opening near the middle to the midpoint probe and alphabetical order to the sortedness requirement; the limit (humans interpolate; binary search probes the exact middle and needs the same sort key) is correct.

tech-divide-conquer-merge.rationale: No analogy: the lesson is a code walk-through of the previous structure and a comparison would repeat the election analogy.

tech-divide-conquer-power.rationale: No analogy: a short algebraic procedure where a comparison would not add understanding.

tech-divide-conquer-karatsuba.rationale: Carpet-fitter analogy: a room with sides (a + b) and (c + d) split into four zones; knowing the two diagonal zones ac and bd, one whole-room measurement minus them gives ad + bc. The mapping is algebraically exact and the limit states it recovers only the sum and that the recursive repetition is what changes growth.

tech-divide-conquer-karatsuba-implementa.rationale: No analogy: implementation detail following the previous unit's analogy.

tech-divide-conquer-closest-proof.rationale: Distanced-guest analogy maps the two-metre rule to the same-half minimum distance and a tile with diagonal under two metres to a delta/2 square; the limit correctly says cross-half points may be closer and that finding them is the strip check.

tech-divide-conquer-closest-code.rationale: No analogy: the conceptual analogy lives in the proof unit; this is an implementation unit.

tech-divide-conquer-practice.rationale: No analogy: a list of engineering notes; the module's divide-and-conquer analogies already cover the idea.

tech-backtracking-state.rationale: Maze-and-chalk analogy (converted from the baseline's inline maze paragraph) maps junctions, corridors and rubbing out marks to choose/explore/unchoose; the limit notes the implicit, generated tree and extra state to restore. Accurate.

tech-backtracking-subsets.rationale: Light-switch panel maps switches to elements and on/off patterns to subsets, which is why each element doubles the count; the limit (each stored subset costs copying and memory) is correct.

tech-backtracking-permutations.rationale: No analogy: the lesson is the code and a factorial count; the subsets analogy already covers enumeration growth.

tech-backtracking-combinations.rationale: No analogy: a short variant of the subsets code.

tech-backtracking-pruning.rationale: Shopping-on-a-budget analogy maps the money left to remaining, the price-sorted shelf to sorted candidates and leaving the shelf to the break; the limit (unsorted or negative values break the shortcut) is correct.

tech-backtracking-duplicates.rationale: No formula and no analogy needed: a one-line rule best shown by the trace.

tech-backtracking-applications.rationale: No analogy: a list of applications and pitfalls.

tech-backtracking-problems-queens.rationale: No analogy: modelling and bookkeeping technique, shown best by the tables.

tech-backtracking-problems-masks.rationale: No formula or analogy needed: a bit-trick implementation of the previous unit.

tech-backtracking-problems-sudoku.rationale: Wedding-seating analogy maps guests to empty cells and acceptable tables to candidate digits, so seating the most constrained guest first is MRV; the limit (ordered commitment and undo, cost of recomputing candidates) is correct.

tech-backtracking-problems-propagation.rationale: Crossword analogy maps entries to variables, fitting words to domains and crossings to constraints; filling a forced entry is a naked single. The limit (a solver records each elimination to restore it) is accurate.

tech-backtracking-problems-word-search.rationale: No analogy: a code walk-through; the maze analogy already covers mark-and-restore.

tech-backtracking-problems-tries.rationale: No formula or analogy needed: a short design note on tries and pitfalls.

tech-greedy-intervals.rationale: No analogy needed: the meeting-room setting is already the concrete scenario.

tech-greedy-exchange.rationale: No analogy: a proof unit whose example is the meeting room itself.

tech-greedy-rooms.rationale: No analogy: rooms are the concrete scenario.

tech-greedy-huffman.rationale: Morse analogy maps letters to symbols and short codes for frequent letters to variable-length coding; the limit correctly says Morse is not a prefix code (E is the start of I) and needs separators. Verified against standard Morse (E ., T -, Q --.-, I ..).

tech-greedy-optimality.rationale: No analogy: a survey and pitfalls unit.

tech-greedy-fails-coins.rationale: No analogy needed: coins are already the familiar setting.

tech-greedy-fails-coin-dp.rationale: No analogy: coins are the familiar setting.

tech-greedy-fails-canonical.rationale: No analogy: a theorem statement and a check.

tech-greedy-fails-fractional.rationale: No formula or analogy needed: the exchange argument is short and the knapsack is itself the concrete picture.

tech-greedy-fails-whole-items.rationale: Car-boot analogy maps the boot to the capacity, bags to indivisible items and loading the most useful-for-size bag first to ratio greedy; the leftover gap is the 20 kg the table shows greedy wasting. The limit (real boots have shape; the model tracks one number, which is why a capacity DP exists) is correct.

tech-greedy-fails-approximation.rationale: No analogy: a survey of guarantees; the car-boot analogy in the previous unit covers the knapsack picture.
